# binary-trees

Allocate and deallocate many binary trees to exercise memory management. Build one "stretch" tree of depth N+1, one long-lived tree of depth N, and for each depth d in 4, 6, ..., N build 2^(N-d+4) short-lived trees of depth d. Print the node-count checksums for each group.

## Input
A single non-negative integer N read as a command-line argument.

## Output
```
stretch tree of depth N+1\t check: <count>
<count>\t trees of depth 4\t check: <sum>
...
long lived tree of depth N\t check: <count>
```

## Invocation
The program is invoked as: <prog> 21

**Default N:** `21` · **Validation N:** `10` · **Algorithm class:** recursive allocation, globally structured
